tools.name: runpod_get_account
tools.description: Get the Runpod account that owns the API key: its id and email. Good first call to confirm which account is connected. GET /v2/account.

tools.name: runpod_get_account_limits
tools.description: Read the spend rate limit, current spend rate and resource limits of the account before deploying. GET /v2/account/limits.

tools.name: runpod_get_balance
tools.description: Read the account balance and billing mode (how much credit is left). GET /v2/billing/balance.

tools.name: runpod_get_billing_history
tools.description: Get total spend over time across Pods, Serverless, storage and clusters, in time buckets. Use last_n for the most recent buckets. GET /v2/billing.

tools.name: runpod_get_pod_billing
tools.description: Get time-bucketed billing for one Pod or for all Pods: GPU, CPU, disk and total. GET /v2/billing/pods.

tools.name: runpod_list_pods
tools.description: List Pods owned by the account, with status, GPU, image and cost fields. Use cursor to get more pages. GET /v2/pods.

tools.name: runpod_get_pod
tools.description: Get one Pod by id: compute, container, storage, networking, lifecycle status and connection details. GET /v2/pods/{id}.

tools.name: runpod_set_pod_state
tools.description: Start or stop one Pod. A stopped Pod is not billed for compute, but its volume disk still bills. Starting a running Pod or stopping a stopped Pod changes nothing. POST /v2/pods/{id}/action.

tools.name: runpod_terminate_pod
tools.description: PERMANENTLY terminate one Pod: compute is released and its host-local persistent storage is destroyed. A network volume is only detached, not deleted. Cannot be undone. Cluster Pods cannot be terminated here. DELETE /v2/pods/{id}.

tools.name: runpod_list_serverless_endpoints
tools.description: List Serverless endpoints owned by the account, with compute, worker limits, scaling and deployment settings. GET /v2/serverless.

tools.name: runpod_get_serverless_endpoint
tools.description: Get one Serverless endpoint by id: compute, workers, scaling, container and current status. GET /v2/serverless/{id}.

tools.name: runpod_list_endpoint_workers
tools.description: List the active workers of one Serverless endpoint, with status, runtime and counts by status. GET /v2/serverless/{id}/workers.

tools.name: runpod_get_endpoint_request_metrics
tools.description: Get request counts, execution time and queue delay of one Serverless endpoint as a time series. GET /v2/serverless/{id}/metrics/requests.

tools.name: runpod_list_templates
tools.description: List the reusable Pod and Serverless templates owned by the account, with container, storage, port and environment settings. GET /v2/templates.

tools.name: runpod_get_template
tools.description: Get one template by id (owned or public): its container and deploy settings. GET /v2/templates/{id}.

tools.name: runpod_list_network_volumes
tools.description: List the persistent network volumes owned by the account, with size, data center and storage tier. GET /v2/network-volumes.

tools.name: runpod_list_gpu_types
tools.description: List GPU types with pricing. Set include_availability to see stock for a product, GPU count and cloud type. GET /v2/catalog/gpus.

tools.name: runpod_list_data_centers
tools.description: List Runpod data centers with region, compliance and storage details. Filter by region or compliance. GET /v2/catalog/datacenters.

tools.name: runpod_list_audit_logs
tools.description: List the audit trail: who did what to which resource and when. Filter by action, actor, time range or search text. GET /v2/audit-logs.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: runpod_get_account · Private data: runpod_get_account · Public sink: runpod_get_account, runpod_set_pod_state · Destructive: runpod_terminate_pod.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: runpod_get_account · Private data: runpod_get_account · Public sink: runpod_get_account, runpod_set_pod_state · Destructive: runpod_terminate_pod

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
